Consonantal i

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

approach verb and noun

come near

also come near, come closer, draw near, go up to, get closer, be coming

classical

Caes. BC 3.9: jamque hiems appropinquābat (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Fam. 2.6.1: cum adpropinquāre tuus adventus putārētur

appropinquō, appropinquāre, appropinquāvī, appropinquātum

verb, first conjugation, with the dative or ad

come near, approach (in place or time)

Of places and of times: winter, a birthday, someone’s arrival.

Examples

  • deinde sēnsim atque placidē, tamquam nōscitābundus, ad hominem accēdit

    then slowly and gently, as if recognising him, it came up to the manGell. 5.14.11

  • itaque iīs ūnctus quī accessit, pungunt

    so if anyone comes near them wearing scent, they stingVarr. RR 3.16.6

  • ubi es? — Ecce mē. accēde ad mē atque adī contrā.

    where are you? — Here I am. Come up to me, come this way.Plaut. Rud. 241–242

Other words

  • accēdō, accēdere, accessī, accessum — go up to, come near

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Gell. 5.14.11: ad hominem accēdit; Plaut. Rud. 242: accēde ad mē

    With ad: to go right up to someone or something.

  • adeō, adīre, adiī, aditum — go to, approach (a person)

    verb, irregular (ad + eō) · also used · classical · Plaut. Rud. 242: accēde ad mē atque adī contrā

    Of going to someone, often to speak to him or ask for something.

  • adventus, adventūs m. — coming, arrival; approach

    noun, fourth declension · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 2.6.1: cum adpropinquāre tuus adventus putārētur

    The noun for someone’s coming.

See also approach, come here, arrive.

SourcesLewis & Short: appropinquo · Lewis & Short: accedo · Lewis & Short: adeo · Lewis & Short: adventus
